title: slash-restart-saves-the-slate-then-hands-off
author: cc
what: A `/restart` skill CC fires on itself: it measures what is behind this session, closes the boundary the way a boundary is closed (a slate through the saveslate door), and then hands off -- either by asking the inner loop to bring this session back, or by standing a new instance up beside it. One word, and the session is on the new build with its continuity written down.
why: Today the act is three commands a tired operator has to remember in the right order, and the order is the whole safety of it: measure, save, then relaunch. Getting it wrong in the other order is a session that ends with nothing written down. Akien, 2026-09-22: 'cairn restart and cairn cc.x restart and slash restart. We only need to have you around to supervise the process the first time.' The skill is the third name, and it is the one CC types.
how: Three steps, in this order and no other. (1) `cairn cc restart status` -- the measurement decides the branch: `inner loop: HOLDING (pid N)` means a loop is behind this session and `now` will bring it back; anything else means there is nothing behind it and `spawn` is the only safe verb. (2) Fire /saveslate -- as a skill, not shelled, because its door demands instruments_read.git_heads matching the live repos and only CC can compile that. A refusal here ABORTS: a restart that relaunched anyway would have spent the conversation to save nothing. (3) Fire the verb the measurement chose. On the `spawn` branch nothing dies -- the skill reports the new instance's remote-control name and STOPS; it must not then kill anything.
traces_to: Law 1 -- the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled: the safe order (measure, save, relaunch) is settled and today has no address but an operator's memory. Also CP4 -- design to the tool: the tool is a CC session that cannot restart itself, and the skill is the one surface that session can reach.
falsifier: GREEN when a session is relaunched by typing one word and the slate written in that act is readable afterward with the pre-restart git heads in its instruments_read. RED if /restart can end a session that has no loop behind it and no spawned replacement already reachable -- a hang-up, the one failure this skill must never cause.

constraints.text: The order is status, then slate, then relaunch -- never slate-then-status. The status decides which relaunch verb is fired, and arming a flag before knowing whether anything can consume it is the hang-up this skill exists to prevent.
A slate refusal aborts the restart. The slate and the relaunch are one act; half of it is worse than none.
Match on HOLDING, and treat every other status output as NONE. The safe branch is the one that kills nothing, so an unparseable status must fall to `spawn`, never to `now`.
/saveslate is FIRED AS A SKILL, never shelled. Its door refuses a packet whose instruments_read.git_heads do not match the live repos, and only a CC session can compile those.
On the spawn branch this session does not end. The skill reports the new instance's remote-control name and stops; killing anything after a successful spawn is out.

This skill relaunches ONE Claude Code process and nothing beneath it. `cairn restart` is the system's restart and does not touch running cc instances (Akien, 2026-09-22); two different acts may not wear one word.

children: none, because the skill is a composition of two things that already exist and are already proved -- cairn/devices/cc/0/bin/restart and skills/saveslate/ -- so there is no part of it that could prove independently before the whole. The one new artifact is the branch selector, and it is the thing the proof at skills/restart/proofs/ drives.
questions: none, because the one spec choice this cast could not settle by itself -- which relaunch verb a session fires on itself -- is settled by MEASUREMENT rather than by his gate: cairn/devices/cc/0/bin/restart prints `inner loop: HOLDING` or `inner loop: NONE` and the skill reads which, so there is nothing here for him to choose. The boundary a cast like this would otherwise have to ask about -- whether relaunching a CC session and restarting the system are one act or two -- he already ruled on 2026-09-22, and ticket 3264ef726e35 carries the other half of that ruling.

watchme.trigger: a new file appears under the superclaude flags home's consumed/ folder -- the restart history, written by the inner loop when it consumes a one-shot flag by MOVING it. The probe fires on the beat that already runs; no poller.
watchme.enough: three consecutive restarts each of which has a slate in CairnCommons/slates/ written within the minute before its consumed stamp, at which point the probe retires. Any single restart with no slate behind it is carried immediately rather than waiting for the third -- that is the failure the skill exists to prevent.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier, naming the consumed flag's stamp and the slate id found (or the explicit absence), so the carry is the pairing rather than a boolean.
watchme.nexus: the hypothesize tree -- a restart with no slate behind it kills the hypothesis that a skill step is enough to make the save happen, and points at physics (the verb refusing to relaunch without one) instead.
watchme.consumer: whoever fires the next /restart, via the cc device's pane -- a restart that lost its slate is a live trouble, not a log line.

links.what: cairn restart cycles the SYSTEM -- the sibling name. Akien ruled the boundary on 2026-09-22: that one does NOT restart the running cc instance(s); this one is the only thing that touches a CC session.

the dispatcher resolves an instance address -- `cairn cc.1 restart`. The third name. /restart fires `cairn cc restart` on instance 0, so it does not wait on that ticket, but the spawn branch's report reads better once `cairn cc.1 restart` resolves.
the verb this skill composes -- status|now|fresh|onexit|spawn|standdown|clear, landed 2026-09-22 in commits da6f8b01 and 6261e14d.
the door the boundary is closed through -- step 2, and the abort condition.

notes.text: So next we build that out. cairn restart and cairn cc.x restart and slash restart. We only need to have you around to supervise the process the first time. Once we know it works we don't have to do any of that. ... No, cairn restart does not restart the running cc instance(s). Otherwise yes, approved all the way to proved.

MEASURED, and it decides which branch gets exercised first: every session alive today was launched by a superclaude that still exec'd claude (the loop landed in da6f8b01, after they started), so `cairn cc restart status` reports NONE for all of them and the FIRST firing of /restart takes the spawn branch. The loop branch stays unmeasured until a session launched after that commit fires it -- which is exactly the supervised first run Akien described.
